info.title: Taskelith execution messages
info.description: Commands to workers and observations from workers over NATS JetStream (G2 decision D3 (a)), and worker heartbeats over core NATS outside any stream. Operations are described from the control plane. Each command, observation, and report is first published with the Nats-Msg-Id header set to its commandId, its observationId, or its reportId and part, and a redrive sets a new one; the identity in the body never changes. A confirmation and a heartbeat are idempotent and have no header. Every message has a JSON encoding of at most 1 MiB. A worker reads the command metadata and payload.protocolVersion first, which keep their meaning across protocol versions, and rejects a command whose version it does not support. Since protocol version 2 (G3 sub-change 9d) the command channel also carries the session commands and the notice of a refreshed per-run SCM credential, and the observation channel the session observations and the adoption confirmation; a message never carries a secret.

workerCommands.description: Commands addressed to one worker, which only that worker can read, through its own durable pull consumer.

installationId.description: The installation that binds the subjects.

workerObservations.description: Observations and reports of one worker, which only that worker can publish.

installationId.description: The installation that binds the subjects.

workerHeartbeats.description: Heartbeats of one worker, which only that worker can publish. Core NATS without a stream: a lost heartbeat is replaced by the next one.

installationId.description: The installation that binds the subjects.

workerId.description: The worker that sends the heartbeat.

Identifier.description: An opaque identifier of 1-128 printable ASCII characters without whitespace.

Instant.description: A UTC time in the form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ.

ContentDigest.description: sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

Generation.description: A compare-and-set generation that starts at 1.

DisplayText.description: Text shown to people and never interpreted, without control characters.

ArtifactRevision.description: An immutable revision of a workflow artifact, identified by artifact and digest.

MessageType.description: Dot-separated lowercase segments, such as sdlc.gate.passed.

CommandMetadata.description: Fields every command carries (architecture section 9). Attempt, worker, and ownership generation are set once an assignment exists (G2); expiry where meaningful.

ProtocolVersion.description: The execution protocol version. A worker executes a command only if it supports the version the command names; the current version is 1.

ProtocolVersionWindow.description: The inclusive range of execution protocol versions a party supports; minimum is at most maximum.

RecoveryEpoch.description: The installation recovery epoch, which starts at 1 and changes when PostgreSQL is restored.

HardControl.description: A resource control a task policy can require as hard.

WorkerCapacity.description: Capacity a worker declares at enrollment and whenever it changes.

ExitStatus.description: An exit code, a terminating signal, or an unknown status.

VersionedCommand.description: The part of every execution command that keeps its meaning across protocol versions; a worker validates it first and rejects an unsupported version.

Sequence.description: A gapless position in one worker journal, starting at 1.

ResourceRequest.description: The CPU, memory, and hard controls reserved for one attempt.

RefusalReason.description: Worker-side refusal reasons of the capacity reservation contract. An offer in an unsupported protocol version is rejected as a command instead.

ProcessIdentity.description: A process, identified by boot, process ID, and start time.

startTime.description: Linux clock ticks after boot, or macOS microseconds.

ObservationMetadata.description: Fields every observation carries. The producer is the pair of workerId and journalId; observationId is deterministic from the observation source. Observations about an attempt require attemptId and ownershipGeneration; a command rejection, an unrecorded process, capacity, admission pressure, and a self-check report are about none.

ObservationsConfirmed.description: The control plane applied every observation of the journal through confirmedThrough. It is not a command and is not journaled.

InventoryRequested.description: Asks the worker for a fresh snapshot of its journal. It is not a command and is not journaled; only the latest request of a worker is current.

requestId.description: A fresh random value for every request, which the snapshot answering it returns.

InventoryReported.description: Sent on every reconnect: the assignments the worker holds and their executions, in parts that together form one snapshot outside the journal sequence.

reportId.description: The same for every part of one snapshot.

requestId.description: The inventory request this snapshot answers, taken after the request arrived.

snapshot.description: Increases with every snapshot of the journal, so that a later one replaces an earlier one.

throughSequence.description: The last journal sequence the snapshot reflects.

InventoryExecution.description: An execution in the worker journal; uncertainty is evidence beside its state.

state.description: launch-intended until the first grant is journaled.

reservation.description: The capacity reservation the assignment holds.

session.description: The attempt's agent session: required from protocol version 2 (`SessionProtocolVersion`), absent at version 1.

AssignmentOfferCommand.description: Offers an attempt to the addressed worker under the capacity reservation it holds.

executionId.description: Set to cancel one execution only, such as an unauthorized start.

CancellationCommand.description: Requests cancellation of the attempt named by the metadata, or of one execution of it. A request is not proof of termination.

AssignmentEndCommand.description: Ends an assignment, so that the worker stops counting it.

AssignmentAcceptedObservation.description: The worker journaled the offer and accepted the assignment.

oneOf.description: Admission pressure, the only retryable refusal, with its causes.

AssignmentRefusedObservation.description: The worker refused an offer it has not acknowledged; the refusal ends the assignment.

CommandRejectedObservation.description: The worker executes nothing of a command it cannot execute, an offer included. It names the command only by its commandId and type, so that no field of an unknown payload is needed.

LaunchRejectedObservation.description: The launch authority returned a non-retryable rejection for an execution.

ExecutionStartedObservation.description: A spawn happened under the claimed launch authorization.

oneOf.description: The spawn failed, so no process of the execution ever ran.

terminationEvidence.description: containment-empty on Linux, process-group-empty on macOS.

oneOf.description: Recovery on start proved the end without an exit status.

ExecutionExitedObservation.description: The whole process set of the execution is proven empty.

ExecutionNotStartedObservation.description: The launch record is sealed: no spawn happened and none can follow.

ExecutionUncertainObservation.description: Neither presence nor absence of the process set can be proven.

TerminationUnprovenObservation.description: The child exited or was cancelled, but processes of the set survive or cannot be ruled out.

UnrecordedProcessObservation.description: A populated containment of this worker has no execution record (Linux, after data loss).

CancellationNotAppliedObservation.description: An adopting supervisor cannot signal safely; the execution stays started for reconciliation.

CapacityDeclaredObservation.description: The capacity and protocol versions the worker declares.

AdmissionPressureChangedObservation.description: The current causes of admission pressure; an empty list clears it.

SelfCheckId.description: A worker admission check: 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, and '-', starting with a letter.

NotApplicableReason.description: Why a check does not apply at this start, derived on the worker from its platform and launch settings.

oneOf.description: The check failed; each detail is a problem.
The check does not apply at this start; the one detail is the reason.

results.description: One result per composed check. A schema cannot require distinct checkIds; the control plane decides a check named more than once as one failed result.

SelfCheckReportedObservation.description: The results of the worker admission checks the worker ran at its start (worker admission contract).

WorkerHeartbeat.description: Sent at a fixed interval to show that the worker is in contact, outside the journal sequence; it is never confirmed or deduplicated.

AgentSessionId.description: A session of the session timeline (`SessionId`), one task's agent session; not a login session.

AgentSessionGeneration.description: A generation of an agent session, one native process, from 1 (`SessionGeneration`).

NativeRequestId.description: The opaque native request ID that the harness port returned.

NativeRequestKey.description: A native request's identity within its session: its generation and native request ID (`RequestKey`).

ClassifiedOperation.description: The plugin's classification of a permission request's native action into a harness-neutral operation (agent harness port contract section 7.2): G3 defines `push` with the full branch ref it pushes to. An unclassified request has none and matches no standing rule.

ref.description: The full branch ref, `refs/heads/` and a branch name.

HarnessText.description: Text of a native request, an output entry, or an answer, at most 65,536 characters (`MAX_HARNESS_TEXT_LENGTH`).

NativeAnswer.description: A consumed answer: a person's or a standing rule's permission answer, a person's input answer, or the host's delegation result (session timeline contract section 5.2).

DelegationResultOutcome.description: A delegated child's outcome in a delegation result (`DELEGATION_OUTCOMES`).

Responder.description: Who gave a consumed answer: a person, a standing rule, or the host.

TurnAuthor.description: A person, or the host with the delegation request whose child's outcome the turn delivers (session timeline contract section 4.1).

TimelinePosition.description: A position in one of a session's ordered lists (turns, native requests, or output), from 1 without gaps.

ExternalId.description: An identifier that an external service issues, compared exactly and never parsed (source control contract section 2, rule 3).

DelegationResult.description: The result of a delegation: pending until the child task ends or the delegation is rejected, then its outcome and summary.

childTaskId.description: The child task that the delegation request named.
The child task that the delegation request named.

DelegationSummary.description: The summary of a delegated child task for its parent, at most `MAX_HARNESS_TEXT_LENGTH` characters; text of the child's run, redacted as that run's text is.

SessionProtocolVersion.description: The execution protocol version of a session command or observation: 2 or later, so that a worker of version 1 rejects it with `execution.command.rejected` and the control plane sends session work only to a worker whose common version is 2 or later.

AssignmentSessionBinding.description: The agent session an offer of protocol version 2 binds its attempt to: the session, its harness, and the model and effort it runs with, and to resume it, its native session and next generation. No credential; the slot credential keeps its own HTTPS channel.

harness.description: The harness plugin (`HarnessPluginId`) that runs the session; a session never changes its harness.

model.description: The harness model the session runs with, set per session.

effort.description: The harness effort the session runs with, set per session.

resume.description: Present to resume the ended session at its next generation; absent, the attempt starts a new session at generation 1.

nativeSessionId.description: The opaque native session ID that the resume keeps.

generation.description: The generation after the session's last one.
The running generation the turn is sent for; the host delivers it in no other.

turn.description: The turn as recorded, with its immutable identity; its text is the recorded, redacted text.

TurnDeliveryCommand.description: Delivers a queued turn to the session's running generation; the control plane sends it only for the turn that `nextDeliverableTurn` returns, one at a time.

ResponseDeliveryCommand.description: Delivers a consumed permission or input answer to the native request it answers, with the approver that gave it: a principal or a standing rule, never the host.

DelegationResultDeliveryCommand.description: Returns an ended delegation's result to the parent's open delegation request; the host is its responder.

ScmCredentialRefreshedCommand.description: A notice that a run's per-run SCM credential has a new version, which the worker fetches with `fetchRunScmCredential`. It never carries a secret.

nativeSessionId.description: The opaque native session ID; a resume keeps it.

GenerationStartedObservation.description: The harness port started or resumed the session's native process.

GenerationEndedObservation.description: The generation ended: the port reported its end, or the host lost it.

TurnDeliveredObservation.description: The port accepted the turn in the named generation.

TurnNotDeliveredObservation.description: The host did not deliver the turn: its generation no longer runs, or the port refused it. The turn stays queued.

TurnEndedObservation.description: The port's `turn-ended`; a failure is present exactly when the outcome is `failed`.

RequestRecordedObservation.description: A native permission, input, or delegation request that the port emitted during a delivered turn; its text is redacted by value on the worker.

ResponseDeliveryReportedObservation.description: The host's one report of delivering a consumed response, a delegation result included, through the port; nothing is resent.

OutputAppendedObservation.description: One chunk of the port's `output` for a delivered turn, redacted by value on the worker; `chunk` numbers the chunks of one generation from 1 without gaps.

LimitSignaledObservation.description: The port's `limit` account signal of the session's slot, with its reset time when known.

ScmCredentialAdoptedObservation.description: The worker fetched the named version and passes it to every later workspace operation of the attempt. The previous version ends only once every attempt of the run that held it adopted this version or a later one, or no longer holds its ownership.

ScmCredentialNotAdoptedObservation.description: The worker did not adopt the named version and keeps its current one: the fetch was refused, a later version was adopted first, or the worker no longer holds the attempt.
